title: Oct 5 Results + Oct 6 Preview: 50-50 Split, But Watch Tomorrow's 63% Play
summary: Oct 5 went 1-1 (50%), but Oct 6 brings a 63% confidence pick in Atlanta

content.value:
## Oct 5 Results: The Numbers Tell the Story

Let's cut straight to the data. October 5th delivered exactly what a coin flip would give you: 1 win, 1 loss, 50.0% accuracy. The model had two picks in play, and we split right down the middle. Not the day we wanted, but the numbers don't lie.

## Breaking Down the Misses and Hits

The Guardians pick at 55% confidence didn't pan out—that's a marginal edge that didn't materialize. But here's the thing about 55% plays: they're supposed to miss 45% of the time. That's literally what the percentage means.

The Rays pick hit at exactly 50% confidence. Essentially a toss-up that broke our way. I'll take it, but I'm not celebrating statistical noise.

The real story? Neither of yesterday's picks cracked 60% confidence. Today's different.

## Oct 6 Preview: Now We're Talking

Forget yesterday's 50-55% range. Tomorrow brings us a 63% confidence play, and the matchup data is compelling. We're looking at Dodgers-Braves, and the model is leaning heavily toward Atlanta.

Yoshinobu Yamamoto takes the mound for LA, while Chris Sale gets the ball for Atlanta. The 63% confidence level puts this firmly in 'strong play' territory—this is where the model has historically shown edge.

## Why 63% Matters

Look at the confidence delta. Yesterday's picks: 55% and 50%. Tomorrow's pick: 63%. That's a 8-13 percentage point jump, which in our model's framework represents a significant edge.

When we're at 63%, we're no longer talking about marginal advantages. The data is showing a clear lean, and that's when you want to pay attention. This is the difference between a slight tilt and a genuine statistical edge.

Tomorrow's slate is lean, but quality over quantity. The Braves pick is where the numbers are pointing.
